fuente.nota: Texto recortado por párrafos; sin cambios en las frases.

parrafos: To trade is to willingly give things or services and get other things or services in return. For example, a person giving a thing must find another person who wants to get that thing. The giver gets something back in return. A trade is sometimes also called an "exchange" or a "swap".

An early type of trade is barter. Barter was the exchange of goods and services for other goods and services. Barter involves trading things without using of money. Modern traders commonly buy and sell by the use of money. Trade between two traders is called bilateral trade. Trade between more than two traders is called multilateral trade.
Services can also be part of a trade. One person can do a job or work for another, and get something in return in a trade.
Money can be given in return for a service or for a thing. If money is part of the trade, then the person who gives the money is buying, and the person who gets the money is selling.

When there is no money involved in the trade, the trade is called barter. If there is money involved in the trade, the trade is called a purchase. In the past, people would barter to get what they wanted, instead of buying goods and services.

Trade occurs not just between people, but also between large companies and even countries. Governments sometimes take some of the money or goods involved in a trade between countries. This is a type of tax called a tariff. Smugglers try to trade without paying tariffs.
Free trade between two countries is when there are small or no tariffs, quotas, or other restrictions on trade. When one country stops all trade with another country, it is called an embargo.

Wholesaling is the sale of goods to industrial, commercial, institutional or other professional businesses. They can also be sold to other wholesalers. It is the sale of goods to anyone that is not a consumer. Wholesalers usually buy and sort goods in large numbers.

Retail is the process of selling goods or services to consumers through many means of distribution to earn a profit. The term "retailer" usually means where a person sells a small amount of good to many individuals, who are consumers.

International trade is the exchange of goods and services between different countries. International trade has existed throughout history. Some examples include Uttarapatha, Silk Road, Amber Road, scramble for Africa, Atlantic slave trade, and salt roads. When there is trade between two or more countries, factors like currency, government policies, economy, judicial system, laws, and markets affect trade.
An entrepôt is a port, city, or trading post where goods may be imported, stored or sold. These cities grew because of the growth of long-distance trade.
resumen_es: Texto divulgativo que define el comercio y sus formas básicas (trueque, compraventa, mayorista y minorista) y presenta conceptos de comercio internacional como aranceles, libre comercio, embargo y puerto franco.
nivel_motivo: Las frases son cortas y sencillas; el nivel léxico sube solo por términos técnicos (tariff, embargo, entrepôt) que el propio texto define.

ideas_clave.idea: Trade means voluntarily exchanging goods or services for something else in return.
The earliest form of exchange was barter, without money, whereas modern exchanges usually involve money and are called purchases; trade may be bilateral or multilateral.
Services as well as goods can be traded, and when money changes hands the payer is the buyer and the recipient the seller.
Countries also trade with each other; governments may levy tariffs on these flows, free trade means few or no barriers, and an embargo halts all trade with a country.
Wholesalers sell large quantities to businesses rather than to consumers, while retailers sell small amounts to individual consumers for profit.
International trade has a long history and depends on factors such as currencies, policies, laws and markets.
Entrepôts are ports or trading centres where goods are imported, stored or sold, and they developed with long-distance trade.

resumen_modelo: The text defines trade as the voluntary exchange of goods or services. Its earliest form was barter, which involved no money, whereas most modern exchanges are purchases in which one party pays and the other sells. Trade also takes place between companies and countries, and governments may intervene by imposing tariffs, removing barriers through free trade or banning exchanges altogether with an embargo. The text then contrasts wholesale, aimed at businesses, with retail, aimed at consumers. Finally, it notes that international trade, shaped by currencies, policies, laws and markets, has existed throughout history and gave rise to trading hubs known as entrepôts.

preguntas.enunciado: Busca en el párrafo 0 dos palabras que el texto usa como sinónimos de «trade».
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word used as another name for 'a trade'.
preguntas.cita: A trade is sometimes also called an "exchange" or a "swap".
preguntas.explicacion: «Exchange» (intercambio) es la palabra neutra; «swap» (cambio, trueque) es más coloquial.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o si el texto no lo dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: Trade between more than two traders is called bilateral trade.
preguntas.cita: Trade between more than two traders is called multilateral trade.
preguntas.explicacion: El comercio entre más de dos partes es multilateral; el bilateral es el que se da entre dos.

preguntas.pregunta: In a trade involving money, who is the seller?
opciones: The person who gives the money
The person who gets the money
The government that collects the tariff
The wholesaler who sorts the goods
respuestas: The person who gets the money
preguntas.cita: the person who gives the money is buying, and the person who gets the money is selling
preguntas.explicacion: Vende quien recibe el dinero; quien lo entrega compra. El Estado y el mayorista no intervienen en esta definición.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o si el texto no lo dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: When money is involved in a trade, the trade is called a purchase.
preguntas.cita: If there is money involved in the trade, the trade is called a purchase.
preguntas.explicacion: El texto lo dice expresamente y lo contrapone al trueque, en el que no hay dinero.

preguntas.pregunta: What is a tariff, according to the text?
opciones: A ban on all trade with another country
A limit on the quantity of goods imported
A tax taken by governments on trade between countries
respuestas: A tax taken by governments on trade between countries
preguntas.cita: Governments sometimes take some of the money or goods involved in a trade between countries. This is a type of tax called a tariff.
preguntas.explicacion: El arancel es un impuesto sobre el comercio entre países. La prohibición total es el embargo y el límite de cantidad es una cuota; los contrabandistas intentan precisamente evitar el arancel.

preguntas.enunciado: Busca en el párrafo 5 una palabra que designe a quienes comercian sin pagar aranceles.
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word for people who trade illegally to avoid tariffs.
preguntas.cita: Smugglers try to trade without paying tariffs.
preguntas.explicacion: «Smugglers» son contrabandistas; el verbo es «to smuggle» y la actividad «smuggling».

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o si el texto no lo dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: Free trade agreements always increase economic growth in both countries.
preguntas.explicacion: El texto define el libre comercio, pero no dice nada sobre sus efectos en el crecimiento económico.

preguntas.enunciado: Busca en el párrafo 6 una palabra que signifique «interrupción total del comercio con otro país».
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word for a situation in which one country stops all trade with another.
preguntas.cita: When one country stops all trade with another country, it is called an embargo.
preguntas.explicacion: «Embargo» en inglés es la prohibición de comerciar con un país; no tiene el sentido jurídico español de «embargo de bienes» (seizure).

preguntas.pregunta: Who do wholesalers NOT usually sell to?
preguntas.cita: It is the sale of goods to anyone that is not a consumer.
preguntas.explicacion: El comercio mayorista se dirige a empresas, instituciones y otros mayoristas, pero no al consumidor final, que es el cliente del minorista.

preguntas.enunciado: Indica si la afirmación es verdadera (V), falsa (F) o si el texto no lo dice (ND).
preguntas.pregunta: Retailers sell small amounts of goods to many individual consumers.
preguntas.cita: a person sells a small amount of good to many individuals, who are consumers
preguntas.explicacion: Es la definición de minorista que da el texto: pequeñas cantidades a muchos consumidores.

preguntas.pregunta: Which of these is given as a historical example of international trade?
preguntas.cita: Some examples include Uttarapatha, Silk Road, Amber Road
preguntas.explicacion: La Ruta de la Seda aparece en la lista. La Liga Hanseática, la ruta de las especias y el canal de Suez son ejemplos reales de comercio, pero el texto no los menciona.

preguntas.pregunta: Why is international trade more complex than trade between two individuals in the same place?
respuestas: Because it involves different countries, so factors such as currencies, government policies, economic conditions, legal systems and markets all influence the exchange.
preguntas.cita: factors like currency, government policies, economy, judicial system, laws, and markets affect trade
preguntas.explicacion: Es una pregunta de inferencia: el texto enumera los factores que afectan al comercio entre países, que no existen en un intercambio local.

preguntas.pregunta: What is an entrepôt and why did such places develop?
respuestas: An entrepôt is a port, city or trading post where goods can be imported, stored or sold. These places grew as long-distance trade expanded.
preguntas.cita: An entrepôt is a port, city, or trading post where goods may be imported, stored or sold.
preguntas.explicacion: La respuesta debe recoger la definición y la causa de su crecimiento: el auge del comercio a larga distancia.
